t: LeetCode 2012 — Sum of Beauty in the Array
o:
## Understanding the problem

Each interior index i (not the first or last element) earns a beauty score: 2 if nums[i] is strictly greater than every element to its left and strictly smaller than every element to its right; otherwise 1 if it is merely strictly greater than its immediate left neighbor and strictly smaller than its immediate right neighbor; otherwise 0. We return the total score.

Example walkthrough: [1,2,3] — index 1 sees prefix {1} all below 2 and suffix {3} all above 2, scoring 2. [2,4,6,4] — index 1: suffix min after it is 4, and 4 is not below 4, so no 2; but 2 < 4 < 6 locally, scoring 1; index 2: 6 is above prefix max 4 yet not below suffix min 4, and locally 6 < 4 fails, scoring 0 — total 1. [3,2,1] scores 0 everywhere.

Constraints: up to 10^5 elements. Comparing each interior index against all neighbors is O(n^2) — risky at this size — while prefix-max/suffix-min tables reduce everything to O(n).
k: Beauty 2 is equivalent to nums[i] > max(prefix) and nums[i] < min(suffix) — checkable in O(1) with precomputed tables.
Beauty 1 is purely local: nums[i−1] < nums[i] < nums[i+1].
All comparisons are strict, so duplicate values block both bonuses, and the two endpoint indices never score.

a.i: For every interior index, scan everything to the left and right to verify the beauty-2 condition, falling back to the local condition otherwise. Straightforward and correct, but each index may trigger two full scans, giving quadratic time.
s: For each interior i, check that every element before i is < nums[i] and every element after i is > nums[i]; add 2 if so.
Otherwise add 1 when nums[i−1] < nums[i] < nums[i+1].
a.t: O(n^2) — up to two full scans per interior index

a.n: Approach 2: Prefix maxima and suffix minima (optimal)
a.i: Precompute sufMin[i] = minimum of nums[i..n−1]. Sweep left to right maintaining runMax = max of nums[0..i−1]. Index i deserves 2 exactly when runMax < nums[i] < sufMin[i+1]; otherwise it deserves 1 when the local strict inequality holds. Each index is judged in constant time after O(n) preprocessing.
s: Build sufMin where sufMin[i] holds min(nums[i:]) (use infinity beyond the last index).
Add 2 when runMax < nums[i] < sufMin[i + 1]; else add 1 when nums[i−1] < nums[i] < nums[i+1].
Update runMax with nums[i] and return the total.
a.t: O(n) — two linear passes: one to build suffix minima, one to score
a.sp: O(n) — the suffix-minimum table (reducible to O(1) with a second reverse pass)

w:
## Wrap-up

Lead with the prefix/suffix framing — recognizing that "greater than all to the left" collapses to one running-max comparison is the core insight. Pitfalls: off-by-one errors around the excluded endpoints (indices 0 and n−1 never score); awarding 1 when the global condition partially held (the 2-check must take priority); forgetting strictness, so plateaus like [1,2,2,3] block bonuses at both copies of 2; confusing sufMin[i] with sufMin[i+1] — the suffix must exclude nums[i] itself. Edge cases: arrays of length 3 (single scored index), monotonic arrays, duplicated maxima/minima. Follow-ups: output per-index beauties, achieve O(1) extra space with two passes, or generalize the local condition to a window of width k.
